chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Isma‘il Al-Anbari, from Yahya ibn Al-Muthanna, from ‘Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu ‘Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
For Al-Qa'im عليه السلام there are two occultations. During one of them, he attends the seasons, sees the people, and they do not see him.

key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: Al-Qa'im, the promised Imam who will rise by the command of Allah
key_terms.الْمَوَاسِمَ: the pilgrimage seasons or recurring sacred gatherings
key_terms.غَيْبَتَانِ: two occultations or two periods of concealment

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the two occultations of Al-Qa'im عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Al-Qa'im عليه السلام will have two periods of ghaybah (occultation). In one of them, he remains present among people during the pilgrimage seasons while remaining unseen by them, highlighting the hidden yet active reality of the Imam's presence.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Ismail Al Anbary, from Yahya Bin Al Musna, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘For Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup> there would be two Occultations. In one of these, he<sup>asws</sup> would be attending the seasons (of Hajj). He<sup>asws</sup> would see the people but they would not be seeing him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 12. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn ’Isma‘il al-Anbari from Yahya ibn al- Muthanna from ‘Abdallah ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurara from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“Al-Qa’im (the one who rise with Divine Authority) will disappear from the public sight twice. In one of them he will attain Hajj. He will see the people but they will not see him.”
